\begin{itemize}\item[1.] A particle moves in the \(x y\)-plane so that its position at any time \(t, 0 \leq t \leq \pi\), is given by \(x(t)=\frac{t^{2}}{2}-\ln (1+t)\) and \(y(t)=3 \sin t\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Sketch the path of the particle in the \(x y\)-plane below. Indicate the direction of motion along the path.
\item[(b)] At what time \(t, 0 \leq t \leq \pi\), does \(x(t)\) attain its minimum value? What is the position \((x(t), y(t))\) of the particle at this time?
\item[(c)] At what time \(t, 0<t<\pi\), is the particle on the \(y\)-axis? Find the speed and the acceleration vector of the particle at this time.
\end{itemize}
\item[(a)]
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/8e3e16eb-a6c0-44e8-b28f-3b7e876998ec-1.jpg?height=502&width=706&top_left_y=706&top_left_x=314)
\item[(b)] \(x^{\prime}(t)=t-\frac{1}{1+t}=0\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& t^{2}+t-1=0 \\
& t=\frac{-1+\sqrt{5}}{2} \text { or } t=0.618 \text { in }[0, \pi] \\
& x(0.618)=-0.290 \quad y(0.618)=1.738
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] \(x(t)=\frac{t^{2}}{2}-\ln (1+t)=0\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& t=1.285 \text { or } 1.286 \\
& x^{\prime}(t)=t-\frac{1}{1+t} \quad y^{\prime}(t)=3 \cos t
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
x^{\prime \prime}(t)=1+\frac{1}{(1+t)^{2}} \quad y^{\prime \prime}(t)=-3 \sin t
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text { acceleration vector } & =<x^{\prime \prime}(1.286), y^{\prime \prime}(1.286)> \\
& =<1.191,-2.879>
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
\(2\left\{\begin{array}{l}\text { 1: graph } \\ \text { 1: direction }\end{array}\right.\)
\(\mathbf{3}\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: x^{\prime}(t)=0 \\ 1: \text { solution for } t \\ 1: \text { position }\end{array}\right.\)
\(4\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: x(t)=0 \\ 1: \text { solution for } t \\ 1: \text { speed } \\ 1: \text { acceleration vector }\end{array}\right.\)
